bug_semantics: The npm/jsDelivr-only 1.17.3 distribution shipped an approximately 76 KiB obfuscated browser crypto-stealer inside eight executable bundles: dist/amp.js, dist/banner.js, dist/creative.js, dist/mobile.js, dist/native.js, dist/native-render.js, dist/uid.js, and dist/video.js. When a publisher loaded 1.17.3 or the then-current `latest`, the injected code ran in users' browsers, hooked fetch, XMLHttpRequest, window.ethereum and other wallet APIs, recognized cryptocurrency addresses and transaction/approval parameters, and silently replaced legitimate destinations with attacker-controlled lookalikes before display or signing.
flaw_origin: Off-repository npm publishing compromise, not a source-tree change. The preserved 1.17.3 package manifest is identical to 1.17.2 for 79 of 88 files; only package.json and the eight generated dist bundles differ, with each affected bundle growing by about 76 KiB. At tag 1.17.2, package.json runs `gulp build` during prepublish, gulpfile.js creates the dist outputs, and .gitignore excludes dist/. The malicious generated artifacts were therefore introduced in the registry publication boundary, for which no Git commit/ref is public.
ai_marker: unavailable: there is no BIC commit object for the npm-only 1.17.3 payload in public Git history, so BIC author, committer, bot identity, Co-Authored-By/Generated-with trailers, and other commit-object AI markers cannot be inspected; no non-BIC commit was substituted for attribution
evidence: First-party advisory https://github.com/prebid/prebid-universal-creative/security/advisories/GHSA-m662-56rj-8fmm identifies exactly affected version 1.17.3, says users of 1.17.3 or then-`latest` (including jsDelivr) received crypto-related malware, lists patched versions as None, says the remediation was npm unpublication, and recommends returning to 1.17.2.

The advisory's referenced incident report, https://www.sonatype.com/blog/npm-chalk-and-debug-packages-hit-in-software-supply-chain-attack, lists prebid-universal-creative 1.17.3 among the additional hijacked packages and says these packages contained the same backdoor; it describes publisher-account takeover and a cryptocurrency-theft payload.

Preserved CDN manifests are reviewer-accessible at https://data.jsdelivr.com/v1/package/npm/prebid-universal-creative@1.17.2 and https://data.jsdelivr.com/v1/package/npm/prebid-universal-creative@1.17.3. A recursive path/hash/size comparison found exactly nine changed paths among 88: package.json (+51 bytes) plus dist/amp.js (+76,139), dist/banner.js (+76,139), dist/creative.js (+76,103), dist/mobile.js (+76,140), dist/native.js (+76,140), dist/native-render.js (+76,139), dist/uid.js (+76,165), and dist/video.js (+76,140). All 79 remaining package files, including source files, have identical hashes.

The campaign's deobfuscated payload and attack path are documented at https://www.aikido.dev/blog/npm-debug-and-chalk-packages-compromised: `checkethereumw` invokes window.ethereum, the code replaces global fetch and XMLHttpRequest methods, `runmask` alters eth_sendTransaction and Solana signing calls, and the analysis explains address/recipient/approval replacement. In the removed PUC package these vulnerable generated-bundle tails are the relevant distribution code; exact PUC artifact line offsets cannot be recovered because the npm/jsDelivr payload is now purged.

Git tag 1.17.2 resolves to full commit 6621f8ecad668de5b5a8accf3b96081573e8bdff (parent e6d61a34307f79a99d49a4f0c7088e8abbf841f1), dated 2025-05-22 and visible at https://github.com/prebid/prebid-universal-creative/commit/6621f8ecad668de5b5a8accf3b96081573e8bdff and https://github.com/prebid/prebid-universal-creative/releases/tag/1.17.2. `git ls-tree -r --long 1.17.2 -- package.json dist` returns package.json only: the vulnerable dist artifacts are absent from this clean tag's Git tree.

At 6621f8ecad668de5b5a8accf3b96081573e8bdff, package.json lines 3-8 identify version 1.17.2, main dist/creative.js, and `prepublish: gulp build`: https://github.com/prebid/prebid-universal-creative/blob/6621f8ecad668de5b5a8accf3b96081573e8bdff/package.json#L3-L8. gulpfile.js lines 120-152 generate/minify files into dist and line 252 assembles the production build: https://github.com/prebid/prebid-universal-creative/blob/6621f8ecad668de5b5a8accf3b96081573e8bdff/gulpfile.js#L120-L152 and https://github.com/prebid/prebid-universal-creative/blob/6621f8ecad668de5b5a8accf3b96081573e8bdff/gulpfile.js#L248-L252. The same tag's .gitignore contains dist/: https://github.com/prebid/prebid-universal-creative/blob/6621f8ecad668de5b5a8accf3b96081573e8bdff/.gitignore.

Full-history mining found tags 1.17.0=8a2482eb5203f108685e31e118c9397de7d2e0bb, 1.17.1=e2b53130632e8aa072d9696f8d87137011b8e71a, 1.17.2=6621f8ecad668de5b5a8accf3b96081573e8bdff, then 1.18.0=d9fe5e47a2c5b9d5d355517614385debcb655f38, with no 1.17.3 ref. `git log --all -S'1.17.3' -- package.json package-lock.json RELEASE_PROCESS.md README.md` returned no commit. Across all 515 reachable commits, `git grep` found none of `checkethereumw`, `newdlocal`, `window.ethereum.request`, the campaign wallet marker `1H13VnQJKtT4HjD5ZFKaaiZEetMbG7nDHx`, or version 1.17.3.

To exclude locally retained deleted history, `git fsck --full --unreachable --no-reflogs` found 395 unreachable commits; each unreachable commit tree was scanned with `git grep` for the same malware markers and version strings, and MATCH_FOUND was 0. Thus neither reachable nor retained unreachable commit history supplies a BIC object or parent tree for the payload.

Registry boundary evidence: https://registry.npmjs.org/prebid-universal-creative currently sets dist-tag `latest` to 1.17.2, omits 1.17.3 from `versions`, retains its historical publish timestamp 2025-09-08T04:08:25.659Z, and contains the later 1.18.0 release whose gitHead is d9fe5e47a2c5b9d5d355517614385debcb655f38. Both https://registry.npmjs.org/prebid-universal-creative/1.17.3 and https://registry.npmjs.org/prebid-universal-creative/-/prebid-universal-creative-1.17.3.tgz return 404; jsDelivr file content also returns 404 although its hashes/sizes remain in the data API. This proves containment by unpublication rather than a source fix commit.

Direct-parent verification is inapplicable rather than positive: no introducer commit exists to have an immediate parent. The clean distribution predecessor 1.17.2 and its tag commit are useful negative controls, but they are not falsely recorded as the parent of an npm publication. Accordingly introducer_parent_absent is false, and both fix SHA fields are null because the first-party fix was a registry operation with no source diff.
reasoning:
Vulnerability-first evidence establishes a malicious distribution lifecycle rather than an ordinary repository bug. Version 1.17.2 is the clean predecessor. On 2025-09-08, npm 1.17.3 changed only package metadata and eight generated browser bundles; those bundles acquired the same approximately 76 KiB crypto-hijacking payload described for the campaign. Loading those files through npm or jsDelivr executed the interceptor in the browser. Maintainers then unpublished 1.17.3 and moved `latest` back to 1.17.2; the advisory explicitly declares no patched version.

A smallest Git BIC cannot be selected. The generated dist files are created by the prepublish build and excluded from Git, there is no 1.17.3 tag/ref or version-string commit, and exhaustive scans of both reachable and retained unreachable commit trees find neither the version nor payload markers. The clean 1.17.2 tag is not an introducer and cannot be repurposed as one; consequently there is also no legitimate immediate-parent tree in which to perform the protocol's vulnerable-line absence test. Likewise, npm unpublication is the direct remediation but has no commit SHA.

AI attribution is therefore blocked at the required BIC-only boundary. Because the causal object was an off-repository registry artifact and its public commit provenance does not exist, inspecting 1.17.2, a later release, a PR, or a fix for AI signals would be non-causal and prohibited. The correct open result is BLOCKED, not NOT_AI and not an AI verdict.
remaining_gap: The precise inaccessible fact is the commit object (if any) that authored the malicious 1.17.3 generated-bundle payload: npm unpublished the version and tarball, jsDelivr purged file contents, and no reachable or retained-unreachable Git commit/ref contains the payload. Without that BIC object there is no direct parent, no commit-object AI marker to inspect, and no source fix SHA; remediation is independently proven as an unpublish/rollback registry operation.
